title: Respiratory Muscle Training in Scleroderma
off: Effects of Respiratory Muscle Training in Patients With Scleroderma With Pulmonary Involvement
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of IMT on respiratory muscle strength, pulmonary function tests, quality of life aerobic capacity, dyspnea, fatigue and physical activity level in scleroderma patients with ILD. The study will include 30 Scleroderma + ILD patients who are under follow-up in Fırat University Rheumatology Department. Patients will be randomly divided into two groups. High intensity intermittent inspiratory muscle training (H-IMT) will be applied to the respiratory muscle training group in addition to the exercise program. Respiratory muscle strength will be assessed by maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and maximal expiratory pressure (MEP); aerobic capacity will be assessed by exercise test and VO2max. Dyspnea will be assessed with the Modified Medical Research Council Scale; fatigue with the Fatigue Severity Scale; quality of life with the Scleroderma Health Assessment Questionnaire; physical activity level with the International Physical Activity Scale - Short Form
desc: Inspiratory muscle training (IMT) is performed by inspiring against an external load provided by a device. It is easy to implement, low cost and can be easily integrated into rehabilitation programs. Pulmonary rehabilitation and inspiratory muscle training have been applied as an effective method in ILD. However, there are no studies investigating the effects of IMT in individuals with ILD. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of IMT on respiratory muscle strength, pulmonary function tests, quality of life, aerobic capacity, dyspnea, fatigue and physical activity level in scleroderma patients with ILD. The study will include 30 Scleroderma + ILD patients who are under follow-up in Fırat University Rheumatology Department. Patients will be randomly divided into two groups. High intensity intermittent inspiratory muscle training (H-IMT) will be applied to the respiratory muscle training group in addition to the exercise program. This training will be performed with Power breath (POWERbreathe Classic Light Resistance, PowerBreath, IMT Technologies Ltd, Birmingham, UK) respiratory muscle training device. In the control group, only stretching, strengthening and posture exercises will be applied as a home program. Respiratory muscle strength will be assessed by maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and maximal expiratory pressure (MEP); aerobic capacity will be assessed by VO2max with exercise test. dyspnea will be assessed using the Modified Medical Research Council Scale; fatigue will be assessed using the Fatigue Severity Scale; quality of life will be assessed using the Scleroderma Health Assessment Questionnaire; physical activity level will be assessed using the International Physical Activity Scale - Short Form.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18-65 years old
* Patients whose medical treatment has not changed in the last three months
* Patients who volunteered to participate in the study and were cooperative
* Literate patients
* Patients followed with a diagnosis of SSc

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who are pregnant
* Patients with a diagnosis of malignancy
* Patients with other concomitant systemic inflammatory rheumatic diseases
* Patients with neurological, orthopedic or congenital problems that prevent physical activity

arms.d: High intensity intermittent inspiratory muscle training (H-IMT) will be applied. This training will be performed with Power breath (POWERbreathe Classic Light Resistance, PowerBreath, IMT Technologies Ltd, Birmingham, UK) respiratory muscle training device. The H-IMT will be performed in seven sets of three-minute cycles consisting of two minutes of training followed by one minute of rest in the training workload. Each session will consist of 14 minutes of loading and seven minutes of rest for a total of 21 minutes.
Stretching exercises for pectoral muscles, neck muscles and back muscles, strengthening exercises for upper extremity and back muscles and posture exercises will be applied.

x.titre: Entraînement des muscles respiratoires dans la sclérodermie avec atteinte pulmonaire interstitielle
x.question: Un entraînement des muscles inspiratoires, ajouté à un programme d'exercices, améliore-t-il la force respiratoire et la fonction chez les patients sclérodermiques avec PID ?
x.contexte:
La pneumopathie interstitielle diffuse (PID) est l'une des principales atteintes graves de la sclérodermie. Elle entraîne dyspnée, fatigue et baisse de la capacité d'effort. La réhabilitation respiratoire est utilisée dans les PID, mais l'entraînement spécifique des muscles inspiratoires y est peu étudié.

L'entraînement des muscles inspiratoires (IMT) consiste à inspirer contre une charge fournie par un dispositif simple et peu coûteux. Cet essai randomisé de l'université de Fırat (Turquie) inclut 30 patients sclérodermiques avec PID. Le groupe IMT effectue un entraînement intermittent à haute intensité avec un appareil POWERbreathe (sept séries de 3 minutes, soit 21 minutes par séance) en plus d'exercices à domicile. Le groupe contrôle ne fait que des étirements, du renforcement et des exercices de posture. Sont évalués la pression inspiratoire maximale (PIM), la pression expiratoire maximale, les EFR, la VO2max, la dyspnée, la fatigue, la qualité de vie et l'activité physique.
x.interet: Si l'IMT améliore la force respiratoire et la capacité d'effort, il pourrait compléter la prise en charge rééducative de la PID sclérodermique. L'effectif est petit et le suivi de 8 semaines.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 65 ans atteints de sclérodermie systémique avec pneumopathie interstitielle.
exclusion: Autre maladie rhumatismale inflammatoire systémique associée
Problème neurologique, orthopédique ou congénital empêchant l'activité physique

bras.traitement: Entraînement inspiratoire intermittent à haute intensité (POWERbreathe), 21 minutes par séance, plus programme d'exercices
Étirements, renforcement des membres supérieurs et du dos, exercices de posture à domicile

x.critere: Force des muscles respiratoires (pression inspiratoire maximale), évaluée sur 8 semaines.
